publicationConclusion.reason: A dated official operative baseline and a dated NBU explanation were actually read. Current Rada metadata identifies the 17 September 2026 edition, but no full current consolidated body or complete 2026 amendment chain was recovered. Do not present older numeric limits as current payment permission.
publicationConclusion.usefulNarrowQuestion: Does money for a separately incorporated U.S. company automatically qualify as maintenance of my Ukrainian company’s own overseas branch?
publicationConclusion.evidenceBoundAnswer: The older NBU point 14(30) expressly concerns the company’s own foreign branches, representative offices and other separate units without creating a separate legal entity, exclusively for their maintenance. The NBU’s 26 August 2026 explanation separately says there is no general resident outward-investment permission and distinguishes branch maintenance and current foreign trade operations. This supports a dated distinction and a question for the servicing bank; it does not prove November 2026 payment eligibility.
publicationConclusion.recommendedPracticalOutput: Before committing to a payment, identify the sender and recipient legal entities, branch-versus-subsidiary structure, exact payment purpose, contract/invoice/budget, currency source and transaction date. Ask the servicing bank to identify the current operative exception and conditions. Do not relabel equity as services or branch maintenance.

olderBranchConditionsAITranslated: The resident legal entity has operated for at least 12 months since state registration before the transaction.
Transfers go to its own foreign branches, representative offices or other separate units without creating another legal entity.
The annual base is €1 million equivalent at the official NBU exchange rate on the transaction date, plus documented 2021 maintenance transfers for eligible units open as of 24 February 2022.
In one calendar month, transfers may not exceed one quarter of the combined annual amount under the preceding two paragraphs.
The company must use its own foreign currency, neither purchased nor raised through credit or a loan.
It must use one chosen servicing bank; changing bank follows a written procedure cross-referenced in the provision.
The exclusive purpose is maintenance of its foreign units, evidenced by an expense budget.
sourcesActuallyRead.paymentScopeCaution: These older conditions are cumulative. The €1 million base is not an arbitrary subsidiary-investment allowance. These numeric conditions have not been verified as current.
sourcesActuallyRead.IPScopeCaution: Older point 14(53) concerns IP protection fees and duties, services of foreign patent offices, and foreign patent attorney services. It does not by itself establish permission for royalties or acquiring IP abroad.
sourcesActuallyRead.incomingInvestmentScopeCaution: Older point 14(57) links a limit to qualifying foreign investment INTO the Ukrainian resident’s capital, with named uses and documents. It is not a general permission to invest abroad.
sourcesActuallyRead.translation: Ukrainian original; English findings are an AI-assisted translation. Extraction shows some PDF column/table artefacts; the relevant point 14(30) wording is fully readable.

AITranslatedFindings: The explanation says Resolution 18 permits only what is expressly allowed during wartime, with different limits, dates and conditions.
As of this post, there was no general permission for residents freely to invest abroad.
The post distinguishes maintenance transfers for foreign representative offices, current foreign-economic operations, and export-contract penalties from general outward investment.
Exceptional government-initiated decisions serving state interests are individual mechanisms, not general currency liberalisation.
sourcesActuallyRead.currentnessCaution: The post is dated 26 August 2026, after Resolution 90 but before Resolution 105. It does not reconcile the latest consolidated law and must remain explicitly dated. It does not establish that all service or IP payments are unrestricted.
